# The Water-Stone of the Wise

But indeed, it is even more wonderful that some men are found who not only inquire into this highest art <note>original: "Eccles. 7", likely referring to the search for the reason of things in Ecclesiastes 7:25</note> but even attempt to handle and practice it, and yet nevertheless they doubt whether it is a natural or rightly magical art, or instead a supernatural and necromantic art <note>necromancy here refers to forbidden "black" magic or communication with the dead</note> acquired only through spirits and illegitimate, prohibited means. Not at all, my good man! Neither the Devil nor any of the impious have that power without divine permission, so as to touch even the smallest part of this art, much less to make it their own or to exercise it according to their own whim. By no means, I say; that art remains in the hand and power of God alone, who bestows it upon whom He wills and simultaneously takes it away again. For into this art, which takes its origin from and out of God, no seekers of pleasure are admitted, much less the dire and infernal spirits; instead, on the other hand, it admits such a spirit as is simple, upright, true, constant, and of a pure and pious essence. Yet the modern world, secure in its impiety, does not recognize this spirit, and therefore remains ignorant of its essence and the highest mystery in many things. For as soon as the world hears anything of it with its ears, yet is unable to comprehend it quickly, then these worldly companions <note>original: "Sapien. 1", referring to Wisdom of Solomon 1:3-5 regarding how wisdom will not enter a deceitful soul</note> call it foolishness. Therefore, because of their blindness, that spirit shall be perpetually hidden from them and at last entirely taken away from them.

<note>A small ink flourish or doodle consisting of several wavy vertical and horizontal strokes appears in the right margin.</note>

Lest I should perhaps proceed further than is just from my purpose with this commemoration, let me touch upon it again and finally bring it to a conclusion. For that reason, I wish to have this properly instilled into pious practitioners <note>term: "artificibus" refers to the alchemical craftsmen or "artists" of the work</note> by way of a friendly exhortation: that to the degree that any man shall establish his heart, soul, indeed his life and actions toward God <note>original: "Eccles. 18 & 29", referring to Ecclesiasticus/Sirach 18:23 and 29:11 regarding preparation for prayer and following commandments</note>, to that same degree shall he perceive a remarkable usefulness daily and even at all hours in the progress of the stone and of his labor. I myself have observed this every day with the highest diligence and great devotion, and have thus experienced it by the very fact. Wherefore, right from the beginning, one ought to direct all his actions toward this and so prepare himself that he may afterwards be able to attain a more happy end in both works.

<summary>The author argues that alchemical success is a divine gift reserved for the pious and upright, rather than a result of black magic or demonic aid. He encourages practitioners to align their lives with God to find success in the creation of the Stone.</summary>
<keywords>divine art, magic vs necromancy, piety, spiritual essence, divine permission, practitioner's conduct, alchemical success</keywords>
